Dollar steady as investors weigh Middle East jitters against softer inflation data - Reuters

briefing.briefing: Right now, the dominant forces pulling on gold are a slightly weaker US dollar (the DXY, which measures dollar strength against a basket of currencies, sits at 101.19), high but gently easing real yields (the 'real yield' is the return investors get after accounting for inflation — at 2.31% on the 10-year, it is still historically high, which usually works against gold), and a modest geopolitical risk backdrop. On the news front, the most relevant headline came roughly 16 hours ago when Reuters reported that gold gained on hopes of de-escalation in the Middle East conflict — that kind of headline typically gives gold a short-lived safe-haven lift, but de-escalation news actually removes a support pillar for gold rather than adding one, so this may have already faded. A second headline from about 19 hours ago noted the dollar was steady as investors weighed Middle East uncertainty against softer inflation data — softer inflation tends to reduce pressure on the Fed to keep rates high, which is mildly supportive for gold. No other headlines in the last 24 hours appear market-moving. Directional bias is NEUTRAL leaning very slightly bullish: gold is trading at $4,084, the Fed is almost certain to hold rates at its July 29th meeting (92% probability), ETF flows [money flowing into gold-backed funds] have been negative for three weeks running, and large speculative traders trimmed their bullish bets last week — none of this screams a strong directional push. Confidence is 4/10; a clear break above recent highs or a fresh geopolitical escalation headline would shift the bias higher, while a dollar rally or a hawkish Fed comment could push it lower. The calendar data shows no scheduled economic events today, and there are no upcoming high-impact events flagged for later this week, which removes a major source of pre-event caution — but it also removes a clear catalyst to spark a big move. On levels, the 14-day Average Daily Range [the typical daily price swing] is $85, and today's range has already used $86.70 of that — meaning the market has essentially hit its average daily move, so a large new directional push today is unlikely and chasing moves at this stage carries extra risk. For trade integration: given the exhausted daily range, neutral positioning, and lack of fresh catalysts, this is a low-conviction environment — if you do trade, reduce your position size and wait for a clean pullback [a temporary dip in an uptrend] on the 5-minute chart before entering, rather than chasing price at current levels. When the daily range is already fully used up, patience is your edge — wait for tomorrow's fresh range to open up before pressing new trades.
